title: Every Hard Year
cues: Every hard year, you was harder than the year
Crimson shekere rhythms pulse through a hazy, golden crowd
intro_or_break
Every time I hit the floor, I looked up, and you was here
Silhouette figures rise from a swirling, dark floor, illuminated by a warm glow
drive
I ain't got a ring big enough to say it right
A vast, empty hand stretches out, grasping a shimmering, oversized key
drive
So I'ma say it the loudest way I know tonight
Bright, layered guitar chords erupt against a deep indigo backdrop, swirling upwards
drive
Lost the job in March, then I lost the car in May
A dusty grey car vanishes into a rain-slicked street, distant and fading
drive
Lost my pride in a line by June, and you stayed
A lone figure stands rigid, consumed by a pulsating, orange-red haze
drive
You took a second shift and never once said "second"
A ghostly second hand spins relentlessly on a dark, antique clock face
drive
Counted rent in quarters on the bed and called it a blessin'
A bed piled with coins glows with a fragile, amber light, reflecting upward
drive
I was ugly to you then, and I ain't cleanin' it up for the song
Dark, smudged hands reach out, obscured by a turbulent, charcoal storm
drive
Slammed doors, slept on the couch, every word I said came out wrong
Doors slam violently, casting jagged shadows across a sparsely furnished couch
drive
You ain't flinch. You set the table, two plates, every night
Two plates shimmer with a soft, white light, set on a dark wooden table
drive
Even when I didn't come to it, my plate sat there in the light
A single plate glows intensely, suspended in a cool, blue-grey illumination
drive
You held the lease, held the phone when the bill man called
Interlocking guitar figures reach across a void, a complex, shifting pattern
drive
Held my head in the bathroom when I couldn't stand at all
A figure collapses, supported by a steady, enveloping, amber light
drive
Held the kids' hands crossin' every street that I was scared of
Hands cradle a child's small form, against a backdrop of deep violet hues
drive
Held it all, and never once asked me what I was made of

drive
Love was you sellin' your grandmama's ring and swearin' you just misplaced it
A hand clutches a tarnished ring, bathed in a mournful, amber glow
drive
Found the pawn ticket in your coat on a Tuesday, sat down in the closet
A dark closet door opens, revealing a crumpled pawn ticket in shadow
drive
Cried like a kid in the dark with your sweaters, then I got up and I bought it
Sweaters swirl around a figure, illuminated by a soft, comforting light
drive
Took me four months, every dollar from the side jobs and the night work
Coins cascade down, forming a shimmering river of gold and silver
drive
Don't look at me. Look at your hand. Yeah. That's what it's worth
A weathered hand rises slowly, reflecting a focused, intense light
drive
I ain't a poet, I'm a man who fell and got picked up

drive
Every hard year, you was the hand, and I was the cup

I'll take the hard ones with you, every bill and every bleedin' sun
